title.narrative: Core support to Cultural Heritage without Borders Kosovo 2023-2027
Kärnstöd till Cultural Heritage without Borders Kosovo 2023-2027

description.narrative:
The mission of CHwB Kosovo is to promote cultural heritage as both a right and a resource. CHwB works with civil society and institutions at all levels to strengthen peace building, sustainable socio-economic and democratic development and the realisation of human rights. CHwB Kosovo is dedicated to promoting the preservation of cultural heritage in areas where the significant cultural heritage is endangered because of economic, social, or political factors.
The focus of the new strategy is related to the irreplaceable role of cultural heritage to face the new challenges in training, creation of sustainable networks of cultural organizations, supporting creative activities, strengthening territorial cultural identities and promoting equal rights for all social groups.
'Everyone has the right to enjoy, access and benefit from cultural heritage' is the impact of the Strategic Plan 2023-2027 of CHwB Kosovo.
This is intended to be achieved through five outcomes'.
OUTCOME 1: Strengthening of regional cultural identities while increasing the partnership between institutions and civil society and mobilising communities in the identification, evaluation and preservation of cultural heritage.
OUTCOME 2: Enabling a bottom-up, critical and creative reflection on intangible heritage by engaging diverse communities and cultural practitioners in research, education and the production of new works and discourses.
OUTCOME 3: Strengthening capacities in the area of built heritage documentation by introducing and adopting advanced technologies.
CROSSCUTTING
OUTCOME 4: Creating equal opportunities for everyone to enjoy and benefit from culture.
OUTCOME 5: Integration of culture heritage in the discourse of environment and energy efficiency.

description.narrative:
By the implementation of extensive nationwide data mapping enabling real-time data input and synchronization - CHwBK have laid a strong foundation for transitioning into analytical and planning phases, positioning CHwB Kosovo as a key actor in integrated, data-driven cultural development. Approximately 900 cultural heritage assets were documented through a structured methodology, including detailed parameters such as condition, accessibility, legal status, and risk factors.
Two Pilot Cultural Districts established institutional cooperation with municipalities, engaged local professionals, and fostered community ownership, as well as collaboration with local actors and NGOs which enabled effective engagement despite sensitive socio-political conditions in northern municipalities. One of these to pilots were focusing on the vineyards in 4 municipalities and the other one on the industrial heritage in northern parts of the country.
In addition, CHwBK has strengthened professional capacities in built heritage documentation through initiatives that focus on integrating advanced digital technologies with traditional conservation practices, addressing both current and future needs of the sector. They have also strengthened their own internal capacities, through staff training, that enhanced their ability to manage, analyse, and visualize heritage data. Overall this has established a strong foundation for a technologically advanced and professionally skilled heritage sector in Kosovo.
A landmark achievement was the implementation of a comprehensive and participatory heritage documentation process in the four northern municipalities where the Serbian community, for the first time, was actively involved in identifying and documenting cultural heritage, supported by local facilitators and community representatives. This contributed to building bridges between communities, institutions, and cultural actors, fostering a more inclusive cultural landscape.
Also the youth camp hosted by CHwB is worth mentioning as it contributed to an inclusive dialogue by bringing together young people from diverse groups in Kosovo: Albanians, Serbs, Bosnians, Roma and Turks.
